title: screening_report_judgement.json -- the screening-report agent's half of the selective lane
description: The agent's contribution to a selective-lane screening report, and nothing else. `run_screening_report.py` assembles the report deterministically from claim_analysis_result.json, evidence_validation_result.json, the conflict ledger and denial_reason_result.json; what it CANNOT derive is which questions matter, who can answer them, and how serious a deferred conflict is. Those three are readings of the case, so they come from the agent through this contract. Added 2026-08-20: the helper had always read this file (`allow_missing=True`) but no schema existed for it, so `write-contract` refused it by name and no run in this repository had ever supplied one -- every selective report silently fell back to the helper's own floor values while reporting success. The fallbacks state facts (a type is unconfirmed, N conflicts were verified) and route them for review; they are not a substitute for this judgement, and a report built on them carries no agent reading at all.

key_issues.description: The issues a 손사/의사 must decide, in the agent's own reading. Spliced into the report as-is, so the ids must be unique within the run.

review_points.description: P3's aggregation point: each flagged claim with the role that can actually answer it. Routed by who can answer, not copied from an upstream contract's reviewer_role.

conflict_severity.description: Severity per deferred conflict, keyed by conflict_id. Only the severity and placement are the agent's; a deferred entry's `professional_summary` was written by consistency-check with the evidence in hand and is copied verbatim by the helper. An empty object is correct when the ledger defers nothing.
